title: D&D Pharmatech's Liver Drug Shows Benefits Before Weight Loss, Lancet Study Finds
excerpt: Zabopegdutide achieved MASH resolution in 62.5% of patients and fibrosis improvement in 50%, with key liver benefits appearing before meaningful weight reduction.
body:
• South Korean biotech D&D Pharmatech's drug zabopegdutide (DD01) showed significant liver improvements before patients experienced meaningful weight loss, published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology
  • At 48 weeks, 62.5% of DD01-treated patients achieved MASH resolution versus 5.3% on placebo, and 50% achieved fibrosis improvement versus 15.8% on placebo
  • Unlike semaglutide-based treatments, DD01 showed rapid liver benefits within 12 weeks through a dual GLP-1/glucagon mechanism that directly targets liver fat
  • The findings could expand treatment options for an estimated 115 million people worldwide living with MASH, a leading cause of liver transplants

D&D Pharmatech's investigational liver drug zabopegdutide has demonstrated significant improvements in liver disease markers before patients experienced meaningful weight loss, according to Phase 2 data published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology. The findings distinguish the drug from existing GLP-1-based treatments like Novo Nordisk's semaglutide, which are widely believed to improve liver outcomes primarily as a consequence of weight reduction.

The South Korea-based biotech's results, drawn from its DD01-DN-02 trial of 67 overweight or obese patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), show that zabopegdutide produced clinically meaningful improvements in liver fat, liver stiffness, and fibrosis biomarkers as early as 12 weeks—before significant weight loss had occurred.

Striking Efficacy Numbers

At 12 weeks, 75.8% of patients treated with zabopegdutide achieved at least a 30% reduction in liver fat, compared to 11.8% on placebo. More notably, 72.7% achieved greater than 50% liver fat reduction, and 48.5% saw complete normalization of liver fat levels. No placebo patient achieved normalization.

The 48-week biopsy data were even more compelling. MASH resolution without worsening fibrosis was achieved in 62.5% of treated patients versus 5.3% on placebo. Fibrosis improvement of at least one stage was seen in 50% of treated patients versus 15.8% on placebo.

"The fact that 50% of patients treated with zabopegdutide experience a one-stage improvement in fibrosis in less than a year is highly encouraging for the hepatology community."

— Mazen Noureddin, MD, Professor of Medicine, Houston Methodist Hospital

Why Weight-Independent Benefits Matter

The critical distinction lies in the drug's dual mechanism. Zabopegdutide targets both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, whereas semaglutide acts only on GLP-1 receptors. The addition of glucagon receptor agonism directly enhances hepatic lipid metabolism and contributes to anti-fibrotic activity within the liver.

Among patients who lost less than 5% of body weight by week 12, zabopegdutide still produced a 37.4% reduction in liver fat and a 19.2% reduction in liver stiffness. Those who lost more weight saw even greater benefits—an 81.1% reduction in liver fat—suggesting the drug works through both weight-dependent and weight-independent pathways.

The MASH Treatment Landscape

MASH affects an estimated 115 million people globally and is a leading cause of liver transplants. Until recently, the only FDA-approved treatments were Madrigal Pharmaceuticals' resmetirom (Rezdiffra) and Novo Nordisk's semaglutide (Wegovy), approved in 2025 for MASH with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis.

Semaglutide resolved steatohepatitis in 63% of patients in the ESSENCE trial, compared to 34% on placebo. Zabopegdutide's 62.5% MASH resolution rate in a smaller trial is comparable, though cross-trial comparisons require caution. The key differentiator is the speed and weight-independence of DD01's liver effects.

What's Next

D&D Pharmatech, which holds FDA Fast Track designation for DD01, presented results at the EASL Congress 2026 in Barcelona and is preparing for late-stage clinical development. The company trades on South Korea's KOSDAQ exchange (347850).
